definitions.E1:
## Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering

The **Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering** is a **four-year, full-time, in-person** program offered at the **Burnaby campus** by the **School of Construction and the Environment**.

### Program overview

The program combines civil engineering theory with practical training in:

- Materials testing
- Surveying
- Manual and computer-aided drafting
- Engineering software
- Design and project work
- Written, graphical, and oral communication
- Construction and project management
- Structural, geotechnical, transportation, municipal, environmental, and water-resource engineering

After successfully completing the first two years, students receive the **Civil Engineering Diploma** credential. Students who meet the continuation requirements may proceed into the final two years of the degree, which include advanced engineering science, design, interdisciplinary studies, and a team-based capstone project.

### Curriculum highlights

**Levels 1–2 — foundation and diploma-stage studies**

- **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**
- **CIVL 1020 — Statistics**
- **CIVL 1024 — Graphical Communication 1**
- **CIVL 1060 — Applied Hydrology**
- **COMM 1142 — Communication for Civil Engineering 1**
- **MATH 1422 — Differential Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 1192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 1**
- **SURV 1130 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 2020 — Mechanics of Materials 1**
- **CIVL 2024 — Graphical Communication 2**
- **CIVL 2025 — Applied Hydraulics**
- **CIVL 2026 — Construction Materials**
- **COMM 2242 — Communication for Civil Engineering 2**
- **MATH 2422 — Integral Calculus for Civil Engineering**
- **PHYS 2192 — Physics for Civil Engineering 2**
- **SURV 2230 — Surveying for Civil Engineering 2**

**Levels 3–4 — advanced diploma/degree preparation**

Courses include:

- **CIVL 3012 — Sustainability in Engineering**
- **CIVL 3020 — Computer Applications**
- **CIVL 3033 — Construction Management 1**
- **CIVL 3041 — Soil Mechanics**
- **CIVL 3050 — Road Design**
- **CIVL 3052 — Municipal Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 3074 — Structural Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 4033 — Construction Management 2**
- **CIVL 4041 — Geotechnical Analysis and Design**
- **CIVL 4052 — Municipal Engineering 2**
- **CIVL 4074 — Structural Engineering 2**
- **CIVL 4090 — Industry Project**

Level 4 also includes a choice of **two electives** from:

- **CHEM 6020 — Chemistry for Civil Engineering**
- **CIVL 4024 — Land Development Modeling**
- **CIVL 4053 — Traffic Engineering Fundamentals**
- **MATH 6010 — Advanced Mathematics for Civil Engineering 1**

**Levels 5–6 — degree-level engineering studies**

Courses include:

- **CIVL 7012 — Computational Methods**
- **CIVL 7021 — Mechanics of Materials 2**
- **CIVL 7060 — Enviromental Engineering**
- **CIVL 7070 — Structural Analysis**
- **ELEX 7355 — The Science of Electronic Sensing and Measurement**
- **MATH 7010 — Advanced Mathematics for Civil Engineering 2**
- **CIVL 7001 — Engineering and Society**
- **CIVL 7011 — Uncertainty in Civil Engineering**
- **CIVL 7020 — Fluid Mechanics and Thermal Science**
- **CIVL 7022 — Structure and Properties of Materials**
- **CIVL 7040 — Geotechnical Engineering 1**
- **CIVL 7092 — Civil Engineering Design**

Students also choose one Liberal Studies elective:

- **LIBS 7005 — Technology, Invention and Power**, or
- **LIBS 7007 — Technology and Society**

**Levels 7–8 — professional practice and capstone**

Courses include:

- **CIVL 7023 — Engineering Dynamics**
- **CIVL 7033 — Project Management in Civil Engineering**
- **CIVL 7062 — Water Quality Engineering**
- **CIVL 7072 — Design of Concrete and Masonry Structures**
- **CIVL 7089 — Capstone Design Proposal**
- **LIBS 7025 — Thinking in Humanities & Social Sciences**
- **MINE 7041 — Geology**
- **CIVL 7030 — Civil Engineering Contracts and Law**
- **CIVL 7050 — Transportation Engineering**
- **CIVL 7090 — Capstone Design Project**
- **OPMT 7031 — Engineering Economics**

Level 7 requires choosing **one technical elective**:

- **CIVL 7063 — Water Resource Engineering**, or
- **CIVL 7073 — Design of Steel Structures**

Level 8 requires choosing **two technical electives** from:

- **CIVL 7042 — Geotechnical Engineering 2**
- **CIVL 7061 — Storm Water Management**
- **CIVL 7074 — Analysis and Design of Timber Structures**
- **CIVL 7075 — Seismic Design**
- **CIVL 7080 — Building Science for Civil Engineering**
- **CIVL 7091 — Civil Engineering Applied Research Project**

### Co-op option

The curriculum also lists optional co-op work terms:

- **CIVL 5990 — Cooperative Education Work Term 1**
- **CIVL 6990 — Cooperative Education Work Term 2**
- **CIVL 7990 — Cooperative Education Work Term 3**
- **CIVL 8990 — Cooperative Education Work Term 4**

These work terms are separate from the academic course requirements.

For the complete current program information, see the institution’s [Civil Engineering Bachelor of Engineering page](https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/).

Successful completion of the first two academic years leads to a **Diploma in Civil Engineering**; continuation into the final two years depends on continuation requirements, which are not detailed in the available record.
- **Courses not shown in the earlier summary include:**
  - **CIVL 1012 — Introduction to Civil Engineering**

  - Choose **two Level 4 electives**.
  - Choose **one Level 7 technical elective**: **CIVL 7063 — Water Resource Engineering** or **CIVL 7073 — Design of Steel Structures**.

https://www.bcit.ca/programs/civil-engineering-bachelor-of-engineering-full-time-8660beng/

definitions.E8: The BEng in Civil Engineering is composed of four years of full-time academic study. The first two years of the degree program present a broad, practical overview of the field of civil engineering, with engineering fundamentals stressed and reinforced across the curriculum. You will receive an abundance of learning opportunities to apply these fundamentals to the solution of real-world design scenarios that would be encountered by both technologists and engineers. Throughout the program, we will present opportunities to strengthen your graphical, written, and oral communication skills. You will spend a significant amount of time on hands-on training in material testing, surveying, manual and computer-aided drafting, and receive instruction in the use of engineering software tools. You will receive a Diploma in Civil Engineering credential upon successful completion of the first two years of academic study within this degree program.  If you meet the continuation requirements, you may continue into the final two years of the degree program which are academically rigorous. We will thoroughly investigate the theoretical foundations of civil engineering science and design topics. At the same time, you will apply the practical civil engineering knowledge you have gained in course assignments and project work. You will also be challenged to view the engineer’s role from an interdisciplinary and multidisciplinary perspective. You will learn about the role of the engineer in project and construction management and enrich your educational experience with complementary studies courses relating to social sciences and the humanities. To further develop your engineering skills for professional practice, you will work with classmates to complete a team-based capstone design project.
